key_insight: CoPoE organizes multimodal Alzheimer’s evidence into interpretable disease axes and fuses only available inputs with a masked Product-of-Experts, enabling missing-modality diagnosis without synthetic imputation.
clinical_relevance: This could help make Alzheimer’s AI more robust in real-world settings where patients often lack one or more test types, while keeping the output more biologically interpretable.
method: Maps each modality into four latent disease coordinates: Risk, Pathology, Neurodegeneration, and Stage (RPNS).
Uses diagonal-Gaussian experts and a masked Product-of-Experts to combine only observed modalities.
Preserves a decomposable posterior for any non-empty modality subset without filling in missing data in the RPNS path.
evidence_signal: On ADNI missing-modality experiments, CoPoE achieved the best all-modality performance and highest mean AUROC across 15 observed-subset evaluations, with improved calibration metrics (ECE, Brier score, and NLL).
watch_item: The approach was evaluated on ADNI and still requires validation across broader cohorts, sites, and clinical workflows before practical deployment.
paper_title: CoPoE: Multimodal Fusion via Decomposable Disease-Coordinate Product-of-Experts for Missing-Modality Alzheimer's Diagnosis
